High risk material

Friable asbestos removal, under enclosure and air monitoring

Removal of friable asbestos: material that can be crumbled by hand when dry. Pipe lagging, loose insulation, sprayed coatings and sheeting that has been damaged badly enough to behave the same way. A different licence class from bonded work, with an enclosure, negative pressure and air monitoring throughout. Send us what you have found, and we will organise licensed removal under enclosure with independent clearance.

0456 220 552

Removal by licensed asbestos removalists. Max holds demolition licence AD214737

Before anything starts

Six things have to be settled first, and not all of them are ours

Most jobs that run late run late on this list rather than on the work itself. Each line says who owns it.

  1. 01

    Survey confirming the material is friable

    Who Max, through an accredited laboratory

    This is the finding that changes the licence class, the method and the cost.

  2. 02

    Class A licensed removalist engaged

    Who Max

    Friable work requires a higher licence class than bonded. We arrange the right contractor.

  3. 03

    Notification

    Who Max, with SafeWork NSW

    Friable removal is notifiable, with a notice period set by the regulation.

  4. 04

    Building vacated for the duration

    Who You

    Not negotiable in most cases. The enclosure and the negative pressure only work if the area is clear.

  5. 05

    Independent assessor engaged

    Who Max

    Air monitoring runs throughout, not only at the end, and it is done by somebody independent of the removalist.

  6. 06

    Power and water available

    Who You

    An enclosure under negative pressure needs both, continuously.

The detail

Why friable work costs what it costs

  • The enclosure is most of the job. Building a sealed enclosure, running it under negative pressure and setting up decontamination is substantial work before any removal starts.
  • The licence class is higher. Friable removal requires a Class A licensed removalist. The pool of contractors is smaller and the controls are heavier.
  • Monitoring runs throughout. Not a single test at the end but continuous monitoring by an independent assessor, which is a separate engagement.
  • The building has to be empty. Which usually means relocation costs that sit outside the removal quote entirely.
  • Clearance is stricter. Visual inspection plus clearance air monitoring before the enclosure comes down, and if it fails, the cleaning repeats.
  • There is often more of it than expected. Lagging follows pipework into subfloors and roof spaces, and the quantity is rarely obvious from the access point.

What we need to quote it

The address

What has to be finished by when, and what is waiting on it

We attend the site before quoting anything substantial.

Found it during a renovation?

Stop. Disturbed friable material in an occupied building is the scenario the controls exist for. Do not continue working in the area and do not attempt to clean it up.

Before you book

What people ask about this one

What is the difference between friable and bonded?
Friable material can be crumbled, pulverised or reduced to powder by hand pressure when dry. Bonded material holds its fibres in a matrix such as cement. The difference decides the licence class, the controls and most of the cost.
Does the building have to be empty?
In most cases yes, for the duration. The enclosure and negative pressure only work if the area is clear, and the risk to anyone in it is the whole reason the controls exist.
Who does the air monitoring?
An independent licensed assessor, engaged separately from the removalist. That independence is the point: the person checking the work is not the person who did it.
How long does it take?
Longer than most people expect, because the enclosure has to be built, the removal done, the area cleaned, the clearance monitoring passed and only then the enclosure dismantled. Each stage has to finish before the next.
Does Max hold the asbestos licence?
No. We hold demolition licence AD214737. The friable removal is carried out by a licensed asbestos removalist of the appropriate class and the clearance is issued by an independent assessor. We manage the pathway so you are not coordinating it yourself.

Tell us where it is and whether it has been disturbed

Whether the material is intact or already damaged is the first question, because it changes the urgency as well as the method. Do not disturb it further to find out.
